name: Vienna
tagline: The schnitzel that overflows the plate, and the original sachertorte with 150 years of history.

Steirereck.description: Considered Austria's best restaurant, inside the Stadtpark. Three Michelin stars.

Hotel Sacher.description: Birthplace of the original sachertorte, celebrating 150 years of history. Anthony Bourdain visited on "No Reservations."

Figlmüller.description: Vienna's most famous schnitzel, so big it overflows the plate.

Naschmarkt.description: Vienna's most famous market, with more than 130 stalls between Karlsplatz and Kettenbrückengasse since the 16th century.

Café Central.description: A historic café since 1876 in the heart of Vienna, once a meeting point for Freud and Trotsky. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

Amador.description: Flagship restaurant of chef Juan Amador, Vienna's second three-Michelin-star venue, set in winemaker Fritz Wieninger's Hajszan Neumann cellar in Grinzing.

Mraz und Sohn.description: Viennese classics reinvented by third-generation chef Lukas Mraz in the Brigittenau district, holding two Michelin stars.

Konstantin Filippou.description: Greek-Austrian chef Konstantin Filippou offers ingredient-focused cuisine with two Michelin stars near Vienna's old town.

TIAN.description: High-end vegetarian cuisine holding a Michelin star and a Green Star for sustainability, led by chef Paul Ivić in the heart of Vienna.

Zum Schwarzen Kameel.description: A delicatessen and wine bar since 1618 on Bognergasse, former purveyor to the imperial court, once frequented by Beethoven.

Griechenbeisl.description: Vienna's oldest restaurant, operating since 1447, with historic guests ranging from Mozart and Beethoven to Mark Twain.

Plachutta Wollzeile.description: A Viennese institution for Tafelspitz (boiled beef), served with the traditional ceremony of specific cuts.

Trzesniewski.description: Tiny open-faced sandwiches in 18 spread varieties since 1902, a Vienna essential founded by Polish cook Franciszek Trzesniewski.

Demel.description: Imperial confectionery founded in 1786 on Kohlmarkt, once purveyor to the court of Franz Josef and Sisi.

Café Hawelka.description: A bohemian café founded in 1939 by Leopold and Josefine Hawelka, a historic meeting point for Viennese writers and artists.

Mayer am Pfarrplatz.description: A Heuriger (wine tavern) in Heiligenstadt, in the very house where Beethoven lived in 1817 and composed part of his Ninth Symphony.

Bitzinger Würstelstand.description: Vienna's most famous sausage stand, beside the Opera and the Albertina; Würstelstand culture became UNESCO Intangible Heritage in 2024.

Skopik & Lohn.description: Contemporary Austrian cooking beneath a striking ceiling scribbled by artist Otto Zitko, featured in the Michelin Guide.

Café Sperl.description: An 1880 Viennese coffeehouse with carambole billiard tables and original Thonet furniture, once a gathering place for the Vienna Secession.

Café Landtmann.description: An 1873 café on the Ring, frequented by Sigmund Freud and Gustav Mahler; one of Vienna's most elegant historic coffeehouses.

Gasthaus Ubl.description: A family-run Beisl of over 50 years in the Wieden district, serving schnitzel, roast pork, and old-school tavern atmosphere.

10er Marie.description: Vienna's oldest Heuriger, documented since 1740, set in centuries-old vaulted cellars in the Ottakring district.

Neni am Naschmarkt.description: Mediterranean-Israeli cooking from the Molcho family that helped turn the Naschmarkt into a culinary destination since opening in 2009.

Zanoni & Zanoni.description: An Italian gelateria founded in 1971 by the Zanoni family at Lugeck, a Viennese classic for gelato.

Urbanek.description: A cheese and cured-meat stall at the Naschmarkt since 1975, visited by Anthony Bourdain on 'No Reservations' and a benchmark for Austrian artisan products.

Kurkonditorei Oberlaa.description: A Viennese patisserie since 1974 on Neuer Markt, celebrated for its top-tier cakes and strudels.

Julius Meinl am Graben.description: The Meinl family's iconic gourmet store on Graben, with a restaurant upstairs and delicatessen goods dating back to the 19th century.

Motto am Fluss.description: A restaurant and café on the Danube Canal at Schwedenplatz, with 1950s-style design and seasonal organic Austrian cooking.

DO&CO Restaurant Stephansplatz.description: A rooftop restaurant atop the Haas Haus with direct views of St. Stephen's Cathedral, serving Austrian-Asian fusion from the DO&CO group.

Café Prückel.description: A 1903 café with Art Deco interiors by Oswald Härdtl, listed as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage since 2011.

Loos American Bar.description: Vienna's first cocktail bar, designed in 1908 by architect Adolf Loos with marble, mahogany, and mirrors.

Aida.description: A pink-branded Viennese café chain founded in 1913, a pioneer of the chain-café format with its own recipes.

Joseph Brot.description: An artisan bakery founded in 2009 that revolutionized Vienna's bread scene with organic ingredients and traditional methods.

Wiener Rathauskeller.description: A historic restaurant in the neo-baroque cellar of Vienna's City Hall, open since 1899.

Café Museum.description: A café designed in 1899 by Adolf Loos, nicknamed 'Café Nihilism' for its minimalist look, once a meeting place for Klimt and Schiele.

Zum Alten Fassl.description: A traditional Beisl in the Margareten district with a courtyard garden, known for its Wiener Schnitzel and Tafelspitz.

Gmoakeller.description: A Viennese tavern of more than 160 years near the Konzerthaus, with vaulted ceilings and classic Austrian cooking.

Ottakringer Brauerei.description: Vienna's last major brewery, founded in 1837, with its own production and guided tours in the Ottakring district.

Wieninger am Stammersdorf.description: The Wieninger family's Heuriger in Stammersdorf, pouring award-winning wines from the Bisamberg and Nussberg vineyards.

Vollpension.description: An intergenerational café where grandmothers and grandfathers bake homemade cakes daily, an award-winning social business near the Naschmarkt.
